cards.question: Customers are not told a retry happened

blocks.paragraph: How much a customer should hear about a retry is a promise to your customers, and only you can decide how much to promise.
When a payment fails and is tried again, the customer is not told. The retry shows on their card statement as a second charge attempt.
A customer may see a second charge attempt on their statement with no explanation.

recommendation.reason: The statement line already names the shop.

cards.question: A payment that fails three times ends with no email

blocks.paragraph: Who tells a customer that their payment could not be taken is a customer-service call, and only you can decide who it comes from and in what words.
After the third failed try the order is given up, and nothing is sent. The customer is left on the checkout page with no message.
A customer whose card keeps failing hears nothing and may think the order went through.

options.label: Keep it
options.consequence: Customers whose card keeps failing hear nothing and may think the order went through; support gets the questions.

options.label: Fix in a follow-up
options.consequence: This ships with customers hearing nothing for now; a follow-up adds the email, once you have chosen its wording.

options.label: Fix before merge
options.consequence: The PR goes back to have the email written first, and returns with a new sheet; the retry ships later.

recommendation.reason: The email needs wording the owner has not chosen yet.

cards.question: Retry for ten minutes after a failure

blocks.paragraph: A failed payment is retried for ten minutes, then the order is cancelled.

options.label: Ten minutes
options.consequence: Orders wait up to ten minutes for a payment to clear.

options.label: One minute
options.consequence: The PR goes back to shorten the window and returns with a new sheet.

recommendation.reason: Most card declines clear within that time.
